Chief_Complaint.content: Worsening itchy, dry, sore, red rash
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Worsening itchy, dry, sore, red rash

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash present for a few days
Rash located on hands and arms
Rash especially bad inside elbows (antecubital fossae)
Rash is very itchy and dry
No scratch marks noted on rash
No thickened skin associated with rash
Over-the-counter hydrocortisone tried for rash and not helping
Prior treatment with OTC cetirizine for rash was ineffective
Patient is not currently using antihistamines

Medications.source_text: Meds: Diprobase cream; Dermal wash; OTC hydrocortisone
Meds: Diprobase cream; Dermal wash; OTC hydrocortisone; blue inhaler PRN

Medications.content: Plan to start Betnovate topical, small amounts fingertip unit twice daily for 2 weeks
Medications.source_text: Start Betnovate topical; small amounts (FTU) BID x 2 wks

Medications.content: Plan to continue emollients Diprobase and Dermal
Plan to continue blue inhaler as needed

Assessment.content: Eczema flare, widespread involving chest, hands, and antecubital fossae
Eczema flare is pruritic, dry, and cracked with no weeping
Eczema flare has suboptimal response to over-the-counter hydrocortisone and prior cetirizine
Assessment.source_text: suboptimal response to OTC hydrocortisone and prior cetirizine

Assessment.content: Asthma is stable with intermittent short-acting beta agonist use

Plan_of_Care.content: For eczema, start Betnovate topical in small amounts fingertip unit twice daily for 2 weeks
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start Betnovate topical; small amounts (FTU) BID x 2 wks

Plan_of_Care.content: For eczema, continue emollients Diprobase and Dermal
If no improvement or any adverse reaction to eczema treatment, patient should contact clinic and call sooner if worsening
